title: Title & Registration Services Late-Registration Penalty: When the Packet Counts as Filed
content:
For a late-registration penalty on a Title & Registration Services order, the penalty filing date is the day the penalty is collected when the state has returned the order for a lien information error on or after the order's most recent submission, because the corrected packet counts as filed only when it goes back; when there is no such lien return and a document was received after the order's most recent submission, it is the date that document was received; otherwise it is the date of the order's most recent remittance to the state.

## Records read

- the state rejection entries on the title order whose reason is lien information error, and the latest of their dates;
- the order's most recent submission date shown on the title order;
- the date of the latest document entry received on the title order;
- the date of the latest remittance entry to the state on the title order.

## Order of application

| Lien information error return dated on or after the most recent submission | Latest document received after the most recent submission | Penalty filing date |
|---|---|---|
| yes | either | the day the penalty is collected |
| no | yes | the date that latest document was received |
| no | no | the date of the most recent remittance to the state |

## Hypothetical illustrations (most recent submission 10 March)

- A lien information error return dated 24 March: the packet counts as filed on the day the penalty is collected.
- No lien return; the latest document was received 15 March: the filing date is 15 March.
- No lien return; the latest document was received 2 March; the most recent remittance is dated 10 March: the filing date is 10 March.
- A document received on 10 March itself is not after the submission.
